posts.title: How do blind people sign their names? Two blind authors sign in two different ways.
posts.description: When one story rules them all, the rest of us become invisible. So let’s lift up more disabled authors. Here are two: Molly Burke, author of Unseen, and me, author of Haben. We signed books for each other before recording an episode of What It’s Really Like . Order Haben Girma’s Book. Order Molly Burke’s Book. posts.title: Being Heumann
posts.description: Being Heumann is the first movie I could access this year. Most films don’t provide descriptive transcripts for Deafblind people. This one does, and the scenes sprang to life under my fingers like a novel. My heart swelled reading how Black Panthers and disabled protesters worked together to outmaneuver the FBI. Being Heumann is one of those cultural touchstones we want to access again and again,

posts.title: My Braille computer is now at the Obama Presidential Center!
posts.description: My Braille computer now lives at the Obama Presidential Center! I hope all students get the opportunity to learn that reading through our fingers is as valid as reading by sight.
